Assumptions

An upgrade to the EOL UUNET network connection (from 12Mbps to 27Mbps) will occur, with minimal impact on most EOL users as it is not the primary link.
User migration activities for applications are scheduled for February 21st at 4:45 PM and require network connectivity.

Assumptions

The SAP Financial Systems will be implemented for the Enron Gas Pipeline Group, Enron North America, and Enron Energy Services companies on July 1, 2000.
The Power mass draft process will be completed by the user deadline of close of business Wednesday.

The conversion to SAP Accounts Receivable (AR) is expected to simplify the Unify/SAP interface, eliminating the need to split bank deposits, interface cash or netting entries back to SAP, or interface payables information from Unify.
Completion of all Service PMAs (PMA related items for ENA and HPLC) will occur by September 18.
Netting processes will be performed within SAP, not Unify, and automatic netting entries will be retained within SAP.
There are no controls in place for the netting process within SAP.
Unify AR will be permanently deactivated, and all Accounts Receivable functions will be performed exclusively in SAP.
Netting is now allowed by legal and credit policies.
The Aug 29-31 offsite meeting will primarily focus on financials and procurement.
SAP's determination regarding user exit disablement (for Brazil and Argentina tax requirements) is pending receipt of tax requirements and/or codes.
GCP has agreed to modify the Bank Partner Type.
Data created in SAP will be correctly captured on the income statement, and SAP will be able to link to this data to retrieve settlement information.
Converted data will not contain settlement period information in the same manner as newly created SAP data.
Overpayments will be classified as "on account," and a case management system will be available to track related issues.
Allowing overapplication of payments in SAP will help account coordinators track overpayments easier than leaving cash on account.
The SAP system and eHROnline will be available for time entry beginning Friday, June 23 at 8:00 AM.
Full SAP functionality for financials will be available on July 5, 2000.
New password criteria will be enforced at initial logon.
Time entry and coding in SAP will accurately populate payroll, projects, and cost centers in real-time.
The system will provide increased flexibility for charging employee and contractor time to actual work areas.
The Xref1 (coordinator) and Xref2 (physical vs. financial flag) fields will be populated as required for the 7/1 go-live.
All intercompany trades will be processed by booking a payable in SAP when payments are received in specific currencies (referring to the three currencies mentioned in the source).
Counterparties will provide their company identification when confirming settlements.
The policy requiring supply verifications for netout customers to be overridden in Unify (to block them in SAP from treasury until payment) will be consistently followed.

1.

The SAP Financial Systems must be implemented for the Enron Gas Pipeline Group, Enron North America, and Enron Energy Services companies by July 1, 2000. 
2.

The system must resolve the current slow performance issue with the "Power mass draft" process to ensure completion by the user deadline of close of business Wednesday. 
3.

The system must simplify the Unify/SAP interface by ensuring bank deposits, cash entries, and netting entries no longer require splitting or interfacing between Unify and SAP. 
4.

5.

All netting of payables and receivables must be performed within SAP, retaining automatic netting entries. 
6.

7.

The system must support Brazil and Argentina tax requirements, potentially by disabling custom user exits, and must allow modification of the Bank Partner Type as agreed by GCP. 
8.

For data created within SAP, the system must allow settlement data to be linked from the income statement side of the entry. 
9.

The system must allow overpayments to be classified as "on account" and support the overapplication of payments to facilitate tracking by account coordinators. 
10.

The SAP system will be available for time entry beginning Friday, June 23, 2000, at 8:00 AM, and full SAP functionality for financials will be available on July 5, 2000. 
11.

The system must support time entry functionality, which populates payroll, projects, and cost centers in real-time, offering flexibility to charge employee and contractor time to actual work areas. 
12.

The system must ensure that the Xref1 (coordinator) and Xref2 (physical vs. financial flag) fields are populated for go-live. 
13.

The system must process intercompany trades by booking a payable in SAP when payments are received in specified currencies and require the provision of company name for settlement confirmations. 
14.
The system must accommodate the policy where supply verifications for netout customers, once finaled in Unify, are overridden and blocked in SAP, preventing treasury pickup until payment.

The SAP Financial Systems are being implemented for the Enron Gas Pipeline Group, Enron North America, and Enron Energy Services companies, with a key go-live date of July 1, 2000 .
Full SAP functionality for financials will be available on July 5, 2000, while SAP and eHROnline became available for time entry on June 23, 2000 .
Support has been provided for navigating this transition period .
A significant decision has been made to permanently discontinue Unify Accounts Receivable (AR), with all AR functions to be performed within SAP .

This change in business logic simplifies the Unify/SAP interface by eliminating the need to split bank deposits, interface cash entries back to SAP, or transfer Unify netting entries and payables information [SOURCE:3, SOURCE:6].

Timekeeping is a focal point of SAP integration, ensuring real-time population of payroll, projects, and cost centers, and offering greater flexibility in charging employee and contractor time .

A new policy mandates that all intercompany trades involving certain currencies will require booking a payable in SAP for incoming payments, and confirming settlements will necessitate providing the company number .
Overpayments are to be classified "on account," highlighting the need for a case management system or allowing overapplication to aid tracking .
For netout customers, a policy is in place to override supply verifications in Unify to block them in SAP from Treasury until payment, following a previous recall issue .
Several constraints and challenges have been addressed.
A software error causing a previous problem has been identified and fixed .
The issue of all service PMAs for ENA and HPLC not being picked up by the Settlements process has been resolved with a fix, with completion expected by September 18 .
Manual processing was required for HPLC PMAs, and missing ENA PMAs were deemed immaterial .
The Power mass draft process is currently running slow but is being completed to meet the user deadline .

Natural Gas, there will be an increased focus on the upstream business, including producers, transporters, and storage providers, utilizing all of ENA's product capabilities [10].
